purpose: The world section of the-reefer.com: the same kind of plain answers as the state pages, for other countries, plus a travel warning list. Every answer names its sources and the date it was checked. A missing answer means not yet reviewed.

Where can adults buy it legally?
How much can an adult carry?

Can you take it across the border?

CA.name: Canada
CA.summary: Legal for adults nationwide since October 17, 2018. Provinces set the age, who sells it and some home-grow rules.

adult-use.short: Yes. 18 federally, 19 in most provinces, 21 in Quebec
adult-use.detail: Federal law sets 18 as the minimum and lets provinces raise it. Ontario, British Columbia and Manitoba use 19, Alberta uses 18 and Quebec raised its age to 21 on January 1, 2020.
adult-use.citation: Cannabis Act (S.C. 2018, c. 16); provincial government pages

medical.short: Yes, through Health Canada
medical.detail: Medical cannabis stays under Health Canada, separate from the provincial rules for non-medical cannabis.
medical.citation: Government of British Columbia; Government of Ontario

buying.detail: Buy from a retailer authorized by your province. Where a province has no retail system, adults can buy online from federally licensed producers. Ontario's online store (OCS.ca) supplies the province's authorized stores.
buying.citation: Department of Justice Canada; Ontario Cannabis Store

possession.short: 30 grams dried in public
possession.detail: Adults can carry up to 30 grams of legal dried cannabis, or the equivalent, in public. British Columbia also caps what a household keeps at home at 1,000 grams.
possession.citation: Department of Justice Canada; Government of British Columbia

sharing.short: Up to 30 grams with another adult
sharing.detail: Adults can share up to 30 grams of legal cannabis with other adults.

home-grow.short: 4 plants per home, except Quebec
home-grow.detail: Federal law allows 4 plants per residence, from licensed seed or seedlings. Quebec bans home growing, and the Supreme Court of Canada upheld that ban in 2023. Manitoba ended its ban on May 1, 2025 and now allows 4 plants per household for people 19 and older.
home-grow.citation: Cannabis Act; Murray-Hall v. Quebec, 2023 SCC 10; Government of Manitoba

border.detail: Cannabis cannot be taken into or out of Canada, including to or from US states where it is legal. This is a federal offence under the Cannabis Act.

driving.short: Criminal THC limits: 2 ng and 5 ng
driving.detail: Having 2 to under 5 nanograms of THC per millilitre of blood within two hours of driving is a less serious criminal offence; 5 ng or more is more serious; and 2.5 ng combined with a blood alcohol of 50 mg per 100 ml is also an offence. There is no medical exemption. Some provinces add zero tolerance: Newfoundland and Labrador allows no detectable THC for novice drivers, commercial drivers and anyone under 22.
driving.citation: Criminal Code and Blood Drug Concentration Regulations; Justice Canada; Government of Newfoundland and Labrador

record-relief.short: Free record suspension for old possession convictions
record-relief.detail: Since August 1, 2019, people convicted only of simple possession of cannabis can apply to the Parole Board of Canada for a record suspension with no fee and no waiting period, without a lawyer. Non-Canadians convicted in Canada can apply too. A record suspension sets the conviction aside but does not erase it, and it does not guarantee entry to another country.
record-relief.citation: Parole Board of Canada; Public Safety Canada

differences.title: What is different about Canada
points: Legal nationwide under one federal law since October 17, 2018, with each province adding its own rules.
The legal age depends on the province: 18 in Alberta, 21 in Quebec, 19 everywhere else.
Each province picks its own store model: government-run, private, or a mix.
Quebec bans home growing, and the Supreme Court upheld that in 2023.
Old possession convictions are set aside by a free record suspension, not erased by expungement.
You still cannot cross the border with it, in either direction.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.summary: Illegal for recreational use. Cannabis is a Class B drug. Specialist doctors have been able to prescribe cannabis-based medicines since November 1, 2018, mostly through private clinics.

adult-use.short: No. Cannabis is a Class B drug
adult-use.detail: Possession carries up to 5 years in prison, an unlimited fine, or both. Supply and production carry up to 14 years.
adult-use.citation: GOV.UK, Drugs penalties

possession.short: Warning or £90 on-the-spot fine for small amounts
possession.detail: Police in England and Wales can give a warning or an on-the-spot fine of up to £90 for cannabis; repeat offences can go up to the maximum. In Scotland, police can issue a Recorded Police Warning for possession instead of reporting it to the prosecutor; the warning still goes on the person's criminal record.
possession.citation: GOV.UK, Drugs penalties; Crown Office (COPFS); Police Scotland via STV News

medical.short: Specialist prescription only, never smoked
medical.detail: Since November 1, 2018, cannabis-based products for medicinal use can be prescribed in England, Wales and Scotland, but only by doctors on the General Medical Council's Specialist Register. Smoking them stays illegal, even with a prescription. GPs cannot start a prescription. Since January 2026, national police guidance approved by the National Police Chiefs' Council tells officers in England and Wales how to deal with prescribed patients.
medical.citation: Home Office Circular 018/2018; Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001 reg. 16A; APCDLO guidance; Chambers 2026 (secondary)

buying.detail: There is no legal sale outside a prescription.
buying.citation: GOV.UK, Drugs penalties

home-grow.short: No. Growing counts as production
home-grow.detail: Growing cannabis is production under the Misuse of Drugs Act, with a maximum of 14 years in prison.
home-grow.citation: GOV.UK, Drugs penalties

driving.short: 2 micrograms of THC per litre of blood
driving.detail: It is an offence to drive with more than 2 µg/L of THC in your blood, whether or not your driving was affected. The limit is set low on a zero-tolerance approach.
driving.citation: GOV.UK, Changes to drug driving law; Road Traffic Act 1988 s. 5A

record-relief.short: No expungement; records become spent
record-relief.detail: There is no process to erase a cannabis conviction. Under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974, a simple caution is spent immediately and a conviction becomes spent after its rehabilitation period. Spent records no longer show on a basic DBS check, but can still show on standard or enhanced checks.
record-relief.citation: GOV.UK, Rehabilitation periods; Disclosing your criminal record

experiment.text: CBD is legal to sell as food only under Food Standards Agency rules. The FSA advises healthy adults to take no more than 10 mg of CBD a day, has set a safe upper limit of 0.07 mg of THC a day, and in September 2026 recommended the first CBD food authorisations to ministers. All CBD products must still comply with the Misuse of Drugs Act.

differences.title: What is different about the United Kingdom
points: Recreational use is a crime, yet medical cannabis has been legal since 2018. One 2026 estimate puts UK patients at about 80,000 to 90,000, most of them through private clinics rather than the NHS.
Prescribed flower has to be vaporised. Smoking it is a crime even with a prescription.
Scotland handles small possession through Recorded Police Warnings set by the Lord Advocate; England and Wales use warnings and £90 fines.
The drug-driving limit for THC is 2 µg/L of blood, among the lowest anywhere.
Old convictions are never erased. They become spent and disappear from basic checks only.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.summary: No legal market. The Supreme Court struck down the total ban on personal use in 2021, but Congress never passed a law, so adults need a permit from COFEPRIS, the federal health regulator, to grow and use their own. Selling is still a crime, and tourists get no protection.
MX.note: Most official sources are in Spanish. Answers summarize them in English.

adult-use.short: Only with a COFEPRIS permit
adult-use.detail: On June 28, 2021 the Supreme Court's full bench struck down the parts of the General Health Law that banned recreational use outright. Congress never wrote a replacement law. COFEPRIS says the ruling only lets an adult use cannabis personally under its health authorization, and does not legalize a market.
adult-use.citation: SCJN Comunicado 187/2021; COFEPRIS statements reported July 2026 (news)

buying.detail: There are no legal shops. COFEPRIS has stated that the court rulings do not authorize selling or distributing cannabis.
buying.citation: COFEPRIS statements reported July 2026 (news)

possession.short: 5 grams is the line in the health law
possession.detail: Under article 478 of the General Health Law, prosecutors do not charge a user who carries no more than the article 479 table amount, which is 5 grams of cannabis. Above that, possession can be charged as narcomenudeo. In February 2026 the Supreme Court protected one man caught with about 14 grams for personal use, but the ruling applied only to his case; the vote fell short of the majority needed to change the rule for everyone.
possession.citation: Ley General de Salud arts. 478 and 479; SCJN, Amparo en Revisión 132/2025; El Cronista (news)

home-grow.short: Only with a COFEPRIS permit
home-grow.detail: A permit lets an adult acquire, plant, grow, harvest, prepare, possess and carry cannabis for personal use only. In 2026 the Supreme Court ordered COFEPRIS to issue permits it had refused, and said the paperwork can be required but cannot be used as a barrier to the right.
home-grow.citation: SCJN Comunicado 097/2026; SCJN case synopsis, Sep 2026; La Razón (news)

medical.short: Yes, under the 2021 regulation
medical.detail: The medical cannabis regulation under the General Health Law was published in the Diario Oficial on January 12, 2021. It covers production, research, manufacturing and medical use, with prescriptions and licenses overseen by COFEPRIS.
medical.citation: Reglamento published in the DOF, January 12 2021

driving.short: No driving high; in Mexico City, 20 to 36 hours in jail
driving.detail: Traffic rules are set locally. In Mexico City, article 50 of the traffic regulation bans driving under the influence of narcotics or psychotropics, with an administrative arrest of 20 to 36 hours that cannot be paid off as a fine, plus six license points.
driving.citation: Reglamento de Tránsito de la Ciudad de México art. 50, via ADN40 (news)

border.short: Never bring cannabis in, even medical
border.detail: The U.S. government warns that drug possession and use, including medical marijuana, is illegal in Mexico and may lead to a lengthy jail sentence.

differences.title: What is different about Mexico
points: Personal use became a right through the courts, not Congress. The Supreme Court ruled in 2021, and lawmakers never followed with a law to regulate it.
The right is real but runs through paperwork. You apply to COFEPRIS for a permit, and people refused have gone back to court to force it to issue one.
There is still nowhere legal to buy. The permit covers growing your own and nothing else.
Without a permit, the 5 gram table in the health law is what separates a user from a dealer. A 2026 attempt to scrap that limit for everyone fell one vote short.
Visitors get none of this. The U.S. government warns that any drug possession, medical cannabis included, can mean a long jail sentence.

DE.name: Germany
DE.summary: Legal for adults since April 1, 2024, without shops. Adults can carry some, grow a few plants at home, or join a non-profit cultivation club.

adult-use.short: Yes, 18 and older
adult-use.detail: The Cannabis Act took effect on April 1, 2024. Since then, adults in Germany can legally use cannabis.
adult-use.citation: Cannabisgesetz (CanG); Federal Government FAQ

buying.detail: Cultivation associations have been allowed to grow since July 1, 2024 and may pass cannabis only to their members. Members get at most 25 grams a day and 50 grams a month; members aged 18 to 20 get at most 30 grams a month, with no more than 10 percent THC.
buying.citation: Federal Ministry of Health FAQ; Federal Government FAQ

medical.short: Yes, under the Medical Cannabis Act
medical.detail: Since April 1, 2024 cannabis is no longer listed under the narcotics law. Medical cannabis is governed by its own law, the Medizinal-Cannabisgesetz (MedCanG).
medical.citation: Federal Ministry of Health, Cannabis als Medizin

border.detail: Bringing cannabis into Germany from abroad remains prohibited.

possession.short: 25 grams in public, 50 grams at home
possession.detail: Adults may carry up to 25 grams in public and keep up to 50 grams at home. Going a little over (up to 30 grams out, up to 60 grams at home) is a fine. Beyond that it is a crime with up to three years in prison.
possession.citation: Federal Government FAQ; Lower Saxony state government

home-grow.short: 3 plants per adult
home-grow.detail: Adults may grow up to three plants at home for their own use. The plants and harvest must be protected from children, teenagers and other people.
home-grow.citation: Federal Ministry of Health, Feb 23 2024; Federal Government FAQ

driving.short: 3.5 ng/ml THC in blood serum; zero for new drivers
driving.detail: Since August 22, 2024 it is an offence to drive with 3.5 ng/ml of THC or more in blood serum. The standard penalty is a 500 euro fine and a one-month driving ban; mixed with alcohol, the standard fine is 1,000 euros. Drivers on probation and anyone under 21 face a total ban, with a standard 250 euro fine. Patients taking prescribed cannabis are exempt.
driving.citation: StVG § 24a (BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 266); Legal Tribune Online; Deutsches Ärzteblatt

record-relief.short: Old convictions can be erased on request
record-relief.detail: Since January 1, 2025, a person convicted under the old narcotics law for something that is no longer a crime can ask the public prosecutor to confirm that the entry can be erased from the federal criminal register. The prosecutor then tells the register to delete it. Lawyers say it is unclear which entries qualify.
record-relief.citation: KCanG §§ 40 and 41; CanG Art. 15; Legal Tribune Online (news)

experiment.text: A federal evaluation called EKOCAN is running until 2028. Its second interim report, on April 1, 2026, found that cultivation clubs still play only a minor role in pushing back the illegal market; the health minister called the law a dud. A separate bill to stop telemedicine prescriptions and mail-order delivery of medical cannabis flower was introduced in December 2025 and was still in Parliament at our last check.

differences.title: What is different about Germany
points: Legal to have and grow, but there are no shops. The only legal sources are your own three plants, a non-profit club, or a prescription.
Where you light up matters. No smoking within 100 metres of the entrance to schools, playgrounds, youth centres or public sports grounds, and none in pedestrian zones between 7am and 8pm.
The clubs have been slow to start. Only 366 had been approved nationwide by October 31, 2025.

Medical cannabis became the easy route instead. Imports of medical flower rose 170 percent from the first to the second half of 2024 as online prescription platforms spread, and the government now wants to restrict them.
Driving has a hard number: 3.5 ng/ml of THC in blood serum, and zero for new and young drivers.
Old convictions for things that are now legal can be wiped from the federal register on request.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.summary: Cannabis is still illegal under the Opium Act, but since the 1970s the state has tolerated small-scale use and sales in licensed coffeeshops. Growing for those shops was never allowed; a state experiment with licensed growers started in 2025.
NL.note: Dutch sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Tolerated, not legal
adult-use.detail: Possessing, selling and growing cannabis are all offences. Prosecutors do not pursue adults for small personal amounts, and coffeeshops that follow the national rules are left alone.
adult-use.citation: Government of the Netherlands; Rijksoverheid

buying.short: Coffeeshops, 5 grams per person per day
buying.detail: A coffeeshop may sell no more than 5 grams per person per day, keep no more than 500 grams in stock and admit only residents of the Netherlands. Whether the residents-only rule is enforced differs from town to town, and each town decides whether to allow coffeeshops at all.
buying.citation: Business.gov.nl; Government of the Netherlands

possession.short: Up to 5 grams is not prosecuted
possession.detail: The Public Prosecution Service does not prosecute people for possessing no more than 5 grams of cannabis.
possession.citation: Government of the Netherlands; Rijksoverheid

home-grow.short: Illegal, but 5 plants are not prosecuted
home-grow.detail: The government says growing cannabis at home or anywhere else is not permitted. Its toleration policy still says prosecutors do not pursue people for no more than five plants. Police can seize the plants.
home-grow.citation: Government of the Netherlands; DutchNews.nl, 2011 Supreme Court ruling (news)

medical.short: Yes, by prescription since 2003
medical.detail: Since September 1, 2003, pharmacies have been able to dispense medicinal cannabis to patients with a doctor's prescription. The government's Office of Medicinal Cannabis supplies standardized, pharmaceutical-grade cannabis, and every Dutch pharmacy can dispense it.
medical.citation: Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research (2018); Al Jazeera, Sep 1 2003 (news)

driving.short: 3 micrograms of THC per litre of blood; zero if combined
driving.detail: Driving under the influence of drugs is prohibited. Since July 1, 2017 there have been fixed blood limits for the most common drugs; for THC the limit is 3 µg per litre of blood. Using several drugs, or drugs with alcohol, triggers a zero limit. Police screen with a saliva test and confirm with a blood test. Two convictions in five years cancel your licence.
driving.citation: Government of the Netherlands; Netherlands Forensic Institute; CBR

experiment.text: The Controlled Cannabis Supply Chain Experiment entered its experimental phase on April 7, 2025, which fixes its end date at April 7, 2029. Coffeeshops in the participating towns may now buy, sell and stock cannabis only from designated growers, and the 500 gram stock limit does not apply to them. Before the experiment ends, the government will decide the future of coffeeshop policy based on the research.

differences.title: What is different about the Netherlands
points: Nothing about cannabis is actually legal. The famous Dutch model is a written promise by prosecutors not to act, under rules known as AHOJG-I: shops may not advertise, sell hard drugs, cause nuisance, admit minors or sell large quantities, and must serve residents only.
The back door problem: coffeeshops may sell, but growing is illegal, so for decades their supply came from the illegal market. The state experiment is the first attempt to fix that.
Tourists can be turned away. Coffeeshops are meant for residents of the Netherlands, though towns decide how strictly to enforce it.
Medical cannabis has been sold in ordinary pharmacies since 2003, earlier than almost anywhere else.
Driving uses a fixed blood limit for THC, with zero tolerance for mixing drugs or drugs and alcohol.

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.summary: The first country to regulate the whole market, under Law 19.172 of December 2013. Citizens and permanent residents register for one of three routes: grow at home, join a club, or buy at a pharmacy. Tourists are shut out.
UY.note: Spanish sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Yes, for registered citizens and residents
adult-use.detail: Law 19.172 regulated home growing, cannabis clubs and pharmacy sales, the first country to do so. Users must register with IRCCA, the national cannabis regulator, and can use only one of the three routes at a time.
adult-use.citation: Ley 19.172 (IMPO guide); EUDA; Pardal et al. (research)

buying.short: Pharmacies: 10 grams a week, 40 a month
buying.detail: Pharmacy sales began on July 19, 2017. Registered buyers may purchase up to 10 grams a week and no more than 40 grams a month, in sealed packs, at prices set by IRCCA. Clubs must have between 15 and 45 members and are licensed and inspected by IRCCA.
buying.citation: Decreto 120/014; IMPO guide to Ley 19.172; EUDA; Ámbito (news)

home-grow.short: 6 plants and 480 grams a year per household
home-grow.detail: Registered home growers may keep up to six flowering plants per household, with a harvest of no more than 480 grams a year, for personal or shared use at home.
home-grow.citation: IMPO guide to Ley 19.172; Government of Uruguay

driving.short: Zero alcohol, and no driving after cannabis
driving.detail: Uruguay's traffic law bars driving with any alcohol in the blood. The cannabis law also bars driving with THC above the permitted level, and the national drug board says drug use must be zero whenever you are going to drive. The government bought 1,000 drug detection devices and trained traffic officers across the country to use them.
driving.citation: Ley 18.191 art. 45; Junta Nacional de Drogas; Infobae 2014 (news)

border.detail: Only citizens and permanent residents can register, so tourists cannot legally buy. In 2026 IRCCA's director said this pushes visitors to the illegal market and that the regulator is designing a way to let them buy.

experiment.text: As of April 30, 2026, 120,083 people were registered: 88,955 pharmacy buyers, 20,798 club members and 10,330 home growers. A government evaluation in 2026 found that 46 percent of consumers now buy through the legal market, and described a remaining gray market made up mostly of unregistered home growers and informal sharing.

differences.title: What is different about Uruguay
points: The state runs it. IRCCA licenses the growers, sets pharmacy prices, registers every user and inspects clubs.
You pick one route. Home grow, club or pharmacy, never two at once.
Your pharmacy has it, maybe. Sales are at ordinary pharmacies that opt in, and in 2017 only 16 of about 1,200 did.
Pharmacy buyers are by far the largest group, almost 89,000 of about 120,000 registered in 2026.
The first legal country is closed to tourists, though the regulator now wants to change that.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.summary: The first country in Asia to decriminalize, in 2022, and the first to pull back. Since June 26, 2025 cannabis flower is a controlled herb, sold only against a prescription. A bill to make cannabis medical-only went to Parliament in September 2026.

adult-use.short: No. Prescription only
adult-use.detail: The government says cannabis is not fully legal. Under the Ministry of Public Health's 2025 notification on controlled herbs, cannabis flower may be bought and sold only with a medical prescription. The narcotics board says a prescription can cover no more than 30 days.
adult-use.citation: Government statement via Thairath; ONCB via The Nation (news)

medical.short: Yes, by prescription from one of seven professions
medical.detail: Licensed shops may sell only to patients with a valid prescription from one of seven recognized practitioners, including medical doctors, Thai traditional medicine doctors, pharmacists and dentists. Since January 2026, every operating dispensary must have a licensed practitioner on site.
medical.citation: Tilleke & Gibbins (law firm); The Nation; Thaiger (news)

buying.short: Licensed shops, prescription only, and shrinking
buying.detail: Shops still trade under three-year licences that expire between 2026 and 2028. The health minister has said more than half of them will need to become medical facilities to renew. More than 7,000 shops have already closed as the rules tightened.
buying.citation: The Nation (news)

border.detail: It is illegal to carry cannabis out of Thailand, and British travellers have been caught doing it, including while transiting. Smuggling carries up to 10 years in prison, and since June 2026 bringing cannabis in can mean up to 10 years and a fine of up to 500,000 baht.

experiment.text: On September 22, 2026 the cabinet approved a draft Cannabis and Hemp Act that would limit cannabis strictly to medical use, require shops to operate as medical facilities and phase out recreational sales. It now goes to the House. In October 2026 the prime minister also proposed tougher penalties through changes to the Narcotics Act.

differences.title: What is different about Thailand
points: Thailand dropped cannabis from its narcotics list in 2022, the first Asian country to do so, and dispensaries spread fast, drawing tourists from countries with tough laws.
Since June 26, 2025 the flower is a controlled herb rather than a narcotic. It is not legal for fun, but it is regulated under traditional medicine law rather than drug law.
Walk-in sales are over. Shops may sell only against a prescription, and they are being pushed toward becoming clinics.
The shop count is collapsing as licences expire, with more than 7,000 closures so far.
Leaving with it is the biggest risk. Travellers have been caught carrying it out, and smuggling carries up to 10 years.

MT.name: Malta
MT.summary: The first EU country to legalize personal use, in December 2021. There are no shops and no legal route for visitors: adults can carry 7 grams, grow four plants at home, or join a licensed non-profit association if they live in Malta.

adult-use.short: Yes, 18 and older, since December 2021
adult-use.detail: Act LXVI of 2021 took effect on December 18, 2021. Since then a person over 18 may have up to 7 grams for personal use without committing an offence. The same law set up ARUC, the Authority for the Responsible Use of Cannabis, to regulate the system.
adult-use.citation: Act LXVI of 2021; Cap. 537 art. 4A; Government of Malta

possession.short: 7 grams on you, 50 grams at home
possession.detail: Adults may carry up to 7 grams. More than 7 and up to 28 grams for personal use goes before a Commissioner for Justice, with a penalty of €50 to €100. At home, up to 50 grams of dried cannabis is allowed. Using it in a public place costs €235, and using it in front of anyone under 18 costs €300 to €500.
possession.citation: Cap. 537 arts. 4A and 7

buying.short: No shops. Non-profit associations, residents only
buying.detail: The only legal supply is a non-profit Cannabis Harm Reduction Association licensed by ARUC; 25 held an operating permit when we checked. Members must be at least 18 and show an identity or residence card issued by the Maltese government, and ARUC says tourists may not become members. A member can get at most 7 grams a day and 50 grams a month, plus up to 20 seeds a month. Each association is capped at 500 members, may not advertise, and must be at least 250 metres from schools, sports facilities and youth centres.
buying.citation: Cap. 537 art. 7A; ARUC; BusinessNow.mt (news)

medical.short: Yes, by prescription since 2018
medical.detail: Any licensed doctor may prescribe medicinal cannabis when there is no viable alternative. Applications are made patient by patient, as directed by the Superintendent of Public Health, and a pharmacist dispenses it at a licensed pharmacy. Preparations may not be meant for smoking. The Malta Medicines Authority publishes the list of approved products.
medical.citation: Cap. 537 art. 10; Superintendence of Public Health; Malta Medicines Authority

home-grow.short: 4 plants per household
home-grow.detail: Adults may grow up to four plants at the home address on their identity card. The limit is four for the household, however many people live there. Plants must be out of public view, out of sight and reach of children, and must not cause a smell nuisance to others. Breaking those conditions costs €300 to €500. Growing up to four plants anywhere other than the registered home costs €700 to €1,000.
home-grow.citation: Cap. 537 art. 7

driving.short: 2 micrograms of THC per litre of blood; random roadside tests
driving.detail: It is an offence to drive with any amount of a drug still in your body. For THC, the law allows drivers of private vehicles up to 2 micrograms per litre of blood; that allowance does not apply to drivers of commercial vehicles, buses, coaches or other passenger-carrying vehicles. Since March 10, 2026 police may demand an oral fluid (saliva) test at random, with no suspicion of the driver needed, and a driver who tests positive for THC can be sent for a blood test. A first conviction brings a fine of at least €4,000 and a driving ban of at least six months; a later one, at least €8,000 and at least a year. Holding a drug control card or a prescription does not exempt a driver.
driving.citation: Traffic Regulation Ordinance (Cap. 65) arts. 15BA, 15CB, 15CC, 15CD and 15H; Act II of 2026; Malta Police

record-relief.short: Yes, by written request
record-relief.detail: A person convicted of something that has since been decriminalised can write to the office that issues conduct certificates and ask for the conviction to be taken off. Once the office confirms the offence has been decriminalised, it must accept the request and remove the entry. The government says no new court application is needed.
record-relief.citation: Conduct Certificates Ordinance (Cap. 77) art. 8A; Government of Malta

border.short: No. Importing is a crime, even for your own use
border.detail: Importing or exporting cannabis without authorisation is an offence, and a court treats importation as dealing unless it is satisfied the drug was only for the person's own use. Even then, the Court of Magistrates can give three to twelve months in prison, a fine of €465.87 to €2,329.37, or both. The law exempts a visitor from criminal liability if they do not live in Malta and, at the first opportunity after landing, hand the drug to a police or customs officer and declare it was for personal use only, in an amount that fits that. A traveller from Spain who arrived with a little cannabis for his holiday, and half a gram of amphetamine, was charged with importation and fined €700. The UK government warns its travellers that drug penalties in Malta can include a ban from the Schengen area of up to five years.
border.citation: Dangerous Drugs Ordinance (Cap. 101) arts. 14, 15A and 22; MaltaToday court report (news); UK FCDO travel advice

sharing.detail: The 2021 reform covers having, growing and getting cannabis from an association. It has no rule letting adults give cannabis to one another, and it leaves the rest of the drug law in place. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, supplying or distributing a drug is dealing, and payment is not part of the definition. The one concession is in sentencing: where a person shared a small amount to be used on the spot, at a single event and for no profit, the court may relax the stricter sentencing rules for dealing, once only.
sharing.citation: Dangerous Drugs Ordinance (Cap. 101) art. 22(1B) and (9); Cap. 537 art. 3

experiment.text: Parliament tightened the law through Act XII of 2025, in force since May 16, 2025. Synthetic cannabinoids such as HHC and THC-P were prohibited, and letting anyone under 18 into an association now costs €3,000 to €10,000. Separately, ARUC lets associations make and hand out resin, by solventless methods only, with one gram of resin counted as three grams of flower toward a member's limits. Regulations made in February 2026 cap the stock at each distribution site by category, from 350 grams to 3.5 kilograms. On November 5, 2026 the home affairs minister said tourists caught smoking cannabis in public would get a €235 on-the-spot fine; the legal notice was still being drafted.

differences.title: What is different about Malta
points: First in Europe. The law took effect on December 18, 2021.
No shops, and nothing for visitors. The legal sources are your own four plants or a non-profit association, and associations are for people who live in Malta.
Small by design. Associations are capped at 500 members and may not advertise or put up signs, and only 25 held an operating permit when we checked.
Smell counts. Since 2025, cannabis odour that causes a nuisance to others carries the same €235 penalty as using it in public, and ARUC inspectors handle complaints about private homes.
Weaker cannabis for the youngest members. ARUC's head said THC must not exceed 18 percent for members aged 18 to 21.
Driving has a hard number: 2 micrograms of THC per litre of blood for private drivers, with random roadside tests since March 2026.
An old conviction for something now decriminalised comes off the conduct certificate on a written request.

The border has a surrender rule. A visitor who hands the drug to police or customs at the first opportunity after landing, and declares it was for personal use, is exempt from criminal liability if the amount fits personal use. Otherwise, bringing it in is importation, a crime.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.summary: Since January 1, 2026, adults over 21 can grow three plants, keep 100 grams at home and carry 25 grams. There are no shops and no clubs, and supplying anyone else is still a crime.
CZ.note: Czech sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Yes, 21 and older, for personal use
adult-use.detail: Since January 1, 2026 a person over 21 needs no permit to keep a limited amount of cannabis or to grow up to three plants for their own use. The change came with Act No. 270/2025, a wider reform of the Criminal Code. Commercial activity is still not permitted.
adult-use.citation: Act No. 167/1998 § 5(12) and (13); Advokátní deník; Radio Prague International; Expats.cz (news)

possession.short: 100 grams at home, 25 grams outside
possession.detail: A person over 21 may keep up to 100 grams of cannabis at home and up to 25 grams elsewhere, for their own use. More than that is a misdemeanour with a fine of up to 50,000 crowns. More than 200 grams at home or 50 grams elsewhere is a crime. Under 21 there is no legal amount: up to 200 grams at home or 50 grams elsewhere is a misdemeanour.
possession.citation: Act No. 167/1998 § 5(12) and § 39; Criminal Code § 285 via Advokátní deník; Expats.cz (news)

home-grow.short: 3 plants, 21 and older
home-grow.detail: A person over 21 may grow, harvest and process up to three cannabis plants for their own use, in a property they own or have another legal right to. More than three plants is a misdemeanour with a fine of up to 50,000 crowns, and more than five is a crime. Under 21, growing up to five plants is a misdemeanour. Extracting resin or THC from the plant is prohibited outside medicine and science.
home-grow.citation: Act No. 167/1998 § 5(13), § 15 and § 39; Criminal Code § 285 via Advokátní deník; Business of Cannabis (news)

buying.detail: There are no shops and no cannabis clubs. The 2026 allowance covers only keeping and growing for your own use. Producing, offering, selling or otherwise supplying cannabis to someone else is a crime under the new section 283a of the Criminal Code.
buying.citation: Criminal Code § 283a via Advokátní deník; Act No. 167/1998 § 5(12) and (13); Expats.cz (news)

sharing.short: No. Supplying someone else is a crime
sharing.detail: The legal amounts are for your own use only. Section 283a of the Criminal Code covers anyone who offers, sells or otherwise supplies cannabis to another person. Separately, enabling a person under 21 to use an addictive substance unlawfully is a misdemeanour.
sharing.citation: Criminal Code § 283a via Advokátní deník; Act No. 167/1998 § 5(12) and § 39(2)

medical.short: Yes, on electronic prescription; insurance pays 90 percent
medical.detail: Doctors prescribe medical cannabis on an electronic prescription to patients over 18, up to 180 grams per 30 days. Public health insurance pays 90 percent of the price for 30 grams a month, and more if the insurer's reviewing doctor approves it. Since April 2025 general practitioners can prescribe it for chronic pain that cannot otherwise be relieved; other conditions stay with specialists.
medical.citation: eRecept guide for doctors (Decree No. 236/2015); ČTK (news)

driving.short: 2 ng/ml of THC in blood; the 2026 reform changed nothing
driving.detail: A driver with 2 nanograms of THC per millilitre of blood or more counts as under the influence, which is at least a misdemeanour: a fine of 7,000 to 25,000 crowns, a driving ban of 6 to 18 months and 6 penalty points. From about 10 ng/ml courts generally treat it as a crime, with up to three years in prison and a ban of up to ten years. Refusing the test brings a fine of 25,000 to 75,000 crowns and an 18 to 36 month ban. The January 2026 cannabis reform left these rules as they were.
driving.citation: Government Regulation No. 41/2014 and Road Traffic Act § 125c via epravo.cz (law firm); Cebia guide (secondary)

record-relief.short: No clearing scheme; unserved sentences are not carried out
record-relief.detail: Our sources describe no erasure of old cannabis convictions. What the reform did is stop punishment: a sentence imposed by December 31, 2025 for something that stopped being a crime on January 1, 2026 is not carried out, including any unserved remainder. The Ministry of Justice says courts apply this on their own, with no application needed, and that it covers some conduct under the old section 285(1), which dealt with growing for personal use.
record-relief.citation: Act No. 270/2025 transitional provision via Ministry of Justice reply MSP-542/2025; Advokátní deník

border.short: No. Import and export are crimes
border.detail: Section 283a of the Criminal Code makes it a crime to import or export cannabis without authorisation, alongside producing and selling it. The 2026 allowance covers keeping and growing for your own use and says nothing about crossing a border.
border.citation: Criminal Code § 283a via Advokátní deník; Act No. 167/1998 § 5(12) and (13)

experiment.text: Cannabis with no more than 1 percent THC counts as technical hemp and sits outside these limits. In July 2025 the government's drug policy office said its working group would keep discussing the proposals that were not adopted. In January 2026 the new justice minister, Jeroným Tejc, said he wants tougher penalties for people who drive or commit other offences under the influence of drugs, including letting courts take away driving licences; as of that report the change was still being prepared.

differences.title: What is different about Czechia
points: You must be over 21. Below that age no amount is legal, though small amounts are a misdemeanour rather than a crime.
Three tiers, not two. Up to 100 grams at home or three plants is legal, the next band is a fine of up to 50,000 crowns, and beyond 200 grams at home or five plants it is a crime.
Nothing to buy. There are no shops and no clubs, and supplying anyone else is a crime under a new cannabis section of the Criminal Code.
Insurance pays for medical cannabis: 90 percent of the price for 30 grams a month.
The reform did not touch driving. The limit stays at 2 ng/ml of THC in blood.
Sentences for acts that stopped being crimes are no longer carried out from January 1, 2026, and courts apply that without an application.

ES.name: Spain
ES.summary: Not legal, but private use and private growing are not crimes. Hundreds of private cannabis clubs operate in a legal gray zone that courts and police are tightening.
ES.note: Spanish sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Private use is not a crime
adult-use.detail: Spain has not legalized cannabis. Using or having drugs in public places, streets, public premises or public transport is a serious administrative offence even when it is not for trafficking, and the Criminal Code punishes growing, making and trafficking. Using and growing for yourself in private is not criminal.
adult-use.citation: Ley Orgánica 4/2015 art. 36.16; Código Penal art. 368; Wikipedia, Cannabis in Spain (compilation)

buying.detail: There are no legal shops. Trafficking in drugs, or otherwise promoting or facilitating their illegal use, is punished with one to three years in prison and a fine of up to twice the drug's value where the substance is not one that causes serious harm to health, and three to six years where it is. Courts may go one grade lower for minor cases. Import of any amount is also a crime.
buying.citation: Código Penal art. 368; Wikipedia, Cannabis in Spain (compilation)

home-grow.short: Not a crime in private for yourself; fined if visible
home-grow.detail: Growing in a place visible to the public is a serious administrative offence, fined €601 to €30,000, unless it amounts to a crime. Growing to supply others is a crime under Article 368. A Murcia court in 2023 upheld one- and two-year prison sentences for a grow of more than 100 plants, calling the number a strong sign of trafficking.
home-grow.citation: Ley Orgánica 4/2015 arts. 36.18 and 39; Código Penal art. 368; El Derecho (news); Wikipedia (compilation)

possession.short: No legal amount in public; fines from €601
possession.detail: Having or using cannabis in a public place brings a fine of €601 to €30,000 and confiscation, even with no intent to sell. Paying within 15 days cuts the fine by half, and a minor's fine can be suspended for treatment or re-education. There is no fixed legal amount. Courts use guideline quantities to separate personal use from supply, about 25 grams for hashish, and judge each case on its facts.
possession.citation: Ley Orgánica 4/2015 arts. 36.16, 39 and 54 and disposición adicional quinta; El Derecho on a 2023 Murcia ruling (news)

medical.short: Hospital-only cannabis preparations since October 2025
medical.detail: Royal Decree 903/2025, in force since October 10, 2025, allows standardised cannabis preparations as pharmacy-compounded formulas. Only hospital specialist doctors may prescribe them, for the indications in the medicines agency's monographs and when authorised medicines do not work well enough, and only hospital pharmacy services prepare and dispense them. The decree covers standardised extracts, with cannabis flower only as the starting material. The agency, AEMPS, keeps a public register of the preparations.
medical.citation: Real Decreto 903/2025 arts. 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9

driving.short: Any presence of drugs: €1,000 and 6 points
driving.detail: Driving with drugs present in the body is an administrative offence: a €1,000 fine and 6 licence points. Driving under the influence of drugs is a crime, with three to six months in prison, or a fine, or 31 to 90 days of community service, plus a driving ban of more than one and up to four years. Refusing the test is also a crime: six months to a year in prison and the same ban.
driving.citation: DGT; Código Penal arts. 379.2 and 383

record-relief.short: General rule: records are cancelled after a crime-free period
record-relief.detail: We found no cannabis-specific scheme. Under the general rule, a person who has completed their sentence has the right to have the criminal record cancelled by the Ministry of Justice after a period without reoffending: six months for light penalties, two years for penalties of up to twelve months, three years for other less serious penalties under three years, five years for less serious penalties of three years or more, and ten years for serious ones. It can be done on request or by the ministry on its own.
record-relief.citation: Código Penal art. 136

experiment.text: Spain's cannabis social clubs are private, members-only associations that rely on the legality of private use and shared cultivation. Their status depends on the case, the judge and the region, and a 2026 study describes their decline after years of growth. Advertising and recruiting tourists are not allowed.

differences.title: What is different about Spain
points: Two tracks and no legal market. In public it is an administrative offence with a fine, supply is a crime, and private use sits in between, unpunished.
The fines are steep. A public-use ticket starts at €601 and can reach €30,000, though paying within 15 days halves it.
No number is safe. There is no legal carry limit; courts work from guideline amounts and the facts of each case.
A plant on the balcony can cost you. Growing where the public can see it is fined on the same scale as public use.
The clubs are tolerated, not licensed. Their status depends on the case, the judge and the region, and they may not advertise or recruit tourists.
Medical cannabis arrived late and narrow: hospital specialists only, from October 2025.
Drivers are punished for presence alone: €1,000 and 6 points, with prison possible when the driving was under the influence.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.summary: Decriminalized all drugs for personal use in 2001. Having cannabis for yourself goes to a health-focused panel, not a court, and since 2023 that holds whatever the amount if personal use is shown. Selling and growing are still crimes.
PT.note: Portuguese sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Decriminalized, not legal
adult-use.detail: Since July 2001, using, buying or having any drug for your own use is an administrative offence, not a crime. Cases go to a regional Commission for the Dissuasion of Drug Addiction, which can recommend treatment, warnings or fines. It is still unlawful: police can seize the drug, and anyone aged 16 or over who is caught is called before the commission.
adult-use.citation: Law 30/2000; U.S. OJP fact sheet; UNSW; Observador (news)

possession.short: 10 days' supply is the reference: 25 grams of herb, 5 of hashish
possession.detail: The reference table sets a daily dose of 2.5 grams of herbal cannabis, 0.5 grams of resin and 0.25 grams of oil, so the 10-day mark is 25 grams, 5 grams and 2.5 grams. Since October 1, 2023 that mark is no longer the line between an offence and a crime. Having more is only a sign that the purpose may not be personal use, and if personal use is shown the case is closed and sent to the dissuasion commission. A 2008 Supreme Court ruling had made larger amounts a crime; Law 55/2023 reversed that.
possession.citation: Portaria 94/96; Law 55/2023 via Dantas Rodrigues and PLMJ (law firms); Harm Reduction Journal (research)

buying.detail: Dealers, traffickers and growers still face criminal penalties. Buying for your own use is itself an administrative offence.
buying.citation: UNSW (research); Decreto-Lei 15/93 art. 40 via Dantas Rodrigues (law firm)

home-grow.short: No. Growing for yourself is still a crime
home-grow.detail: Growing cannabis for your own use carries up to three months in prison or a fine of up to 30 day-units, though the court may waive the penalty. The 2023 reform decriminalized having and buying for personal use, not growing.
home-grow.citation: Decreto-Lei 15/93 art. 40 as amended by Law 55/2023, via Dantas Rodrigues and PLMJ (law firms)

medical.short: Yes, on prescription from a pharmacy, since 2019
medical.detail: Law 33/2018 and Decree-Law 8/2019 allow cannabis-based medicines and preparations approved by the medicines agency, INFARMED. A doctor may prescribe them only when conventional treatments with authorised medicines do not work or cause relevant side effects, and they are dispensed in pharmacies. INFARMED's list of approved uses took effect on February 1, 2019: spasticity from multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injury, nausea from chemotherapy and similar treatments, appetite stimulation in palliative care, chronic cancer or nerve pain, Tourette syndrome, severe childhood epilepsy and treatment-resistant glaucoma.
medical.citation: INFARMED Deliberação 11/CD/2019 (Lei 33/2018; Decreto-Lei 8/2019)

driving.short: Banned under the influence; fine of €500 to €2,500
driving.detail: The Highway Code bans driving under the influence of psychotropic substances. A driver counts as under the influence when a medical or forensic report says so after testing, and the fine is €500 to €2,500. It becomes a crime, with up to a year in prison or a fine of up to 120 day-units, when the driver is not in a condition to drive safely.
driving.citation: Código da Estrada art. 81 via Pplware (secondary); Código Penal art. 292 via Tribunal da Relação de Coimbra, 2022

experiment.text: The 2023 change is contested. In January 2026 Madeira's regional parliament voted to ask the national parliament to restore a presumption of trafficking for anyone holding more than the 10-day amount, arguing that the reform made small-scale dealing harder to prosecute. It is a proposal, not law. In practice, a lawyer quoted by Observador in 2023 put fines at about 50 to 100 euros, and the paper reported that a person who follows the commission's plan is not fined.

differences.title: What is different about Portugal
points: Decriminalized is not legal. Use and possession are administrative offences handled by health-focused commissions instead of courts.
It covers every drug, not just cannabis, and has since July 2001.
Quantity no longer decides it. Since October 2023, more than 10 days' supply is a warning sign, not an automatic crime.
Growing is the exception. Growing for yourself is still a crime, even though having it is not.
Police can still take it. It is not a crime, but it is not lawful either.
Medical cannabis is a pharmacy product on prescription, for a short list of conditions.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.summary: Illegal above 1% THC, but up to 10 grams for personal use is not punished and using it is a 100 franc fine. About 10,000 adults buy legally through official city pilot trials, and a law for regulated access is still in committee.
CH.note: German sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Illegal, but small amounts are tolerated
adult-use.detail: Cannabis with 1% THC or more is prohibited outside the official pilot trials. An adult caught using it can get a fixed penalty of 100 francs, while having up to 10 grams for personal use is not a criminal offence. Enforcement still differs from canton to canton. About 10,400 adults were in the seven ongoing trials as of June 2025.
adult-use.citation: FOPH; ch.ch; FOPH pilot trial analysis; Chambers 2026

buying.detail: The trials sell regulated cannabis to registered participants. The Bern, Biel and Lucerne pharmacy trial has been extended to October 2028. Outside the trials, only products under 1% THC, such as high-CBD flowers for smoking, can be sold and bought legally.
buying.citation: FOPH; Swissinfo (news)

possession.short: Up to 10 grams is not punished
possession.detail: Having up to 10 grams for your own use is not a criminal offence and is not fined. Using it can still bring the 100 franc fixed penalty. Minors come under juvenile criminal law.
possession.citation: FOPH; ch.ch

sharing.short: Passing up to 10 grams to an adult is not fined
sharing.detail: Supplying up to 10 grams to another adult, such as sharing a joint, is not fined. Selling it is not allowed.

home-grow.short: Only hemp under 1% THC
home-grow.detail: Growing your own is allowed only if the plant stays below 1% THC. Cannabis at or above that level is prohibited outside the pilot trials.
home-grow.citation: ch.ch; FOPH

medical.short: Yes, on a doctor's prescription since August 2022
medical.detail: The ban on cannabis for medical purposes was lifted on August 1, 2022. Doctors can prescribe cannabis medicines without a special permit from the health office, and pharmacies make up preparations on prescription. Patients usually pay themselves, because compulsory health insurance covers the cost only in exceptional cases. Doctors must report treatment data for the first two years, a requirement that runs until 2029.
medical.citation: FOPH, Medizinische Anwendung von Cannabis; ch.ch

driving.short: Zero tolerance: 1.5 micrograms of THC per litre of blood
driving.detail: Driving with THC in your blood is not allowed. Switzerland treats proven THC as unfit to drive whatever the concentration, using an analytical limit of 1.5 micrograms per litre of whole blood with a 30 percent margin for measurement uncertainty. Legal low-THC hemp can still leave measurable THC. People taking prescribed THC products get an individual fitness assessment instead.
driving.citation: ch.ch; Swiss Society of Legal Medicine report for the Federal Roads Office (2023)

border.short: Swiss-legal hemp can be illegal next door
border.detail: Other countries, including Switzerland's neighbours, have stricter laws and lower THC limits, so products that are legal in Switzerland may be prohibited abroad. The government's advice is to check with the authorities of the country you are travelling to before taking any cannabis product with you.

experiment.text: A National Council committee drafted a Cannabis Products Act that would give adults legal, strictly regulated access, and put it out for consultation from August 29 to December 1, 2025. On May 8, 2026 the committee voted 16 to 8, with one abstention, to keep working on it and sent the draft back to its subcommittee for revision; it reported that a majority of cantons reject the draft in its current form. It is not law.

differences.title: What is different about Switzerland
points: The line is 1% THC, higher than in neighbouring countries. Below it, hemp flowers are sold and bought legally.
Using it is fined, having it is not. An adult caught using can get a 100 franc penalty, while up to 10 grams for personal use is not punished.
Legal cannabis exists only inside research. About 10,400 adults were buying it through seven pilot trials in mid-2025.
Cantons differ. The federal health office says the fixed penalty has only partly made enforcement uniform.
Zero tolerance at the wheel, and legal hemp can still leave THC in the blood.
A legalization bill exists, but the committee sent it back for revision in May 2026.
Medical cannabis needs no special permit since 2022, but patients usually pay for it themselves.

IL.name: Israel
IL.summary: One of the world's largest medical programs per person, with about 140,000 licence holders in 2024. Recreational use is illegal, but personal amounts of up to 15 grams are handled with fines.
IL.note: Hebrew sources are summarized in English.

medical.short: Yes, by licence or prescription
medical.detail: The Israeli Medical Cannabis Agency at the Ministry of Health, set up in 2011, licenses patients and the whole supply chain. Since April 1, 2024, patients with chronic pain or PTSD still need a licence, while those with other recognized conditions, including cancer, epilepsy, Crohn's disease, multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's, get a prescription instead. About 140,000 people held licences in 2024, up from about 33,000 a decade earlier. Cannabis is not in the government health basket.
medical.citation: Herzog Fox & Neeman (Chambers guide); Leumit health fund; Ynetnews; Jerusalem Post

adult-use.short: Illegal, but small amounts are a fine, not a crime
adult-use.detail: Using cannabis without a medical licence violates the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance. Since April 2022, personal use of up to 15 grams is handled with an administrative fine rather than a criminal charge, including for people with a criminal record and for repeat offences. Soldiers, prison guards and police officers in compulsory service are excluded, and so are minors.
adult-use.citation: Ynet on the Knesset Constitution Committee, Mar 23 2022 (news); Leafly (news); Wikipedia (compilation)

possession.short: Up to 15 grams: 500 shekels in private, 1,000 in public
possession.detail: For personal use of up to 15 grams, the fine is 500 shekels for having or using it in a non-public place and 1,000 shekels for using it in public, as approved by the Knesset Constitution Committee in March 2022. We could not confirm whether those amounts have changed since.
possession.citation: Ynet on the Knesset Constitution Committee, Mar 23 2022 (news)

home-grow.short: No. Growing is prosecuted
home-grow.detail: Police have charged home growers with growing a dangerous drug or with possession not for personal use. A 2017 internal police order, reported by Haaretz, said that growing small amounts at home for personal use would under certain conditions be treated as the lesser violation of personal use. The order was internal, and its conditions were not published.
home-grow.citation: Haaretz, Dec 4 2017 (news)

buying.detail: Patients with a licence present it at pharmacies authorized by the Ministry of Health. Outside the medical program there is nothing legal to buy.
buying.citation: Leumit health fund; Herzog Fox & Neeman (Chambers guide)

record-relief.short: By request to the pardons department
record-relief.detail: In March 2022 President Isaac Herzog and Justice Minister Gideon Sa'ar invited people convicted of cannabis possession or personal use to ask for their criminal records to be erased, and people with pending cases to ask for the charges to be dropped. Each request is decided on its merits. It does not cover people charged with other offences alongside cannabis, or people who were soldiers or minors when arrested. Requests go through the Pardons Department page of the Justice Ministry website. We could not confirm that the route is still open.
record-relief.citation: Cannabis Business Times; Leafly (news), March 2022

experiment.text: On May 3, 2026 the Health Ministry published the recommendations of a committee led by Dr. Gilad Bodenheimer: phase out smoked medical cannabis over three years in favor of extracts or precision inhalers, start patients on low doses with low THC, and move all treatment to the health funds, which would get about a year to prepare. The ministry said the recommendations are not immediately binding.

differences.title: What is different about Israel
points: Medical first. Licences grew from about 33,000 to about 140,000 in roughly a decade.
Recreational use is illegal but mostly a fine. Up to 15 grams for personal use brings an administrative fine instead of a criminal charge.
Not everyone gets the fine-only track. Soldiers, prison guards, police officers in compulsory service and minors are left out.
Old records can be erased on request, after a 2022 call from the president and the justice minister.
The medical program is tightening. A ministry committee wants smoked cannabis phased out within three years.
Patients pay. Cannabis is outside the government health basket.

AU.name: Australia
AU.summary: Adult use is illegal almost everywhere. The exception is the Australian Capital Territory, where adults may keep up to 50 grams and grow two plants at home, though nothing can be sold or shared. Medicinal cannabis is prescribed nationwide and dispensed by pharmacies.
AU.note: Each state and territory writes its own drug laws, so check the place you are in. Dollar amounts are Australian dollars.

adult-use.short: Only in the Australian Capital Territory
adult-use.detail: Since January 31, 2020, adults 18 and over in the Australian Capital Territory, which includes Canberra, may possess small amounts and use it at home. Using it in public is still an offence there. Everywhere else adult use is illegal, and selling is illegal in every state and territory. Commonwealth law also applies across Australia, including the ACT, and ACT Policing says its officers can use either law.
adult-use.citation: ACT Government, Cannabis; ACT Policing, Drugs and the law; healthdirect, Cannabis (reviewed Feb 2026)

medical.short: Yes, by prescription through a pharmacy
medical.detail: A doctor or other registered prescriber can prescribe medicinal cannabis anywhere in Australia. Most products are unapproved medicines, so the prescriber first goes through the Therapeutic Goods Administration's Special Access or Authorised Prescriber scheme, and may also need approval from the state or territory health department. A doctor can apply to prescribe it for any condition but may have to show evidence it is likely to help. A pharmacist dispenses the product. Only one cannabis medicine, for certain kinds of epilepsy, is subsidised by the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme, so most patients pay the full price, which healthdirect says can run to thousands of dollars a year.
medical.citation: health.gov.au, Other ways to access medicines; healthdirect, Medicinal cannabis (reviewed Feb 2026); Better Health Channel, Victoria (reviewed 2019)

buying.detail: No shop anywhere in Australia may sell cannabis for adult use. That includes the ACT, where selling stays illegal even from home. The only lawful purchase is a prescribed medicinal product dispensed by a pharmacist.
buying.citation: ACT Government, Cannabis; healthdirect, Cannabis and Medicinal cannabis (reviewed Feb 2026)

possession.short: 50 grams in the ACT; an offence elsewhere
possession.detail: Adults in the ACT may hold up to 50 grams of dried cannabis or 150 grams of fresh cannabis. Possession is illegal in New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, Western Australia and Tasmania. In South Australia and the Northern Territory a small amount is not a criminal offence but can bring a fine. A University of New South Wales review of the rules as of May 2024 put South Australia's fine at A$250 to A$400 for up to 100 grams, and found police elsewhere can caution or divert instead of charging: under 30 grams in New South Wales, up to 50 grams in Victoria and Queensland, and up to 10 grams in Western Australia.
possession.citation: ACT Policing, Drugs and the law; healthdirect, Cannabis (reviewed Feb 2026); UNSW Drug Policy Modelling Program, Bulletin No. 31, June 2024 (research)

sharing.short: No. Even a gift is an offence in the ACT
sharing.detail: The ACT allows personal possession only. Selling, sharing or giving cannabis to another person is an offence there, and that covers plants and seeds. It is illegal to distribute cannabis in every other state and territory as well.
sharing.citation: ACT Policing, Drugs and the law; ACT Government, Cannabis; healthdirect, Cannabis (reviewed Feb 2026)

home-grow.short: Two plants per adult in the ACT only
home-grow.detail: Adults in the ACT may grow up to two plants each at home, with a maximum of four per household. Hydroponics and other artificial cultivation are an offence, and so is growing where the public can reach the plants. Growing is illegal in every other state and territory, and healthdirect says that applies to people with a prescription too.
home-grow.citation: ACT Policing, Drugs and the law; ACT Government, Cannabis; healthdirect, Medicinal cannabis (reviewed Feb 2026)

driving.short: Any THC is an offence in NSW, Victoria and the ACT
driving.detail: It is illegal to drive under the effects of cannabis in every state and territory, and a positive roadside test for THC brings penalties. In New South Wales, Victoria and the ACT the offence is having any THC present, impaired or not. In New South Wales and Victoria that applies to patients with a prescription too, and the ACT applies its rule even though possession is legal there. In New South Wales a first offence currently brings a fine and a three-month licence suspension. Tasmania's law is different: there is no offence when the drug was obtained and administered in line with the state's Poisons Act. A South Australian MP told parliament in March 2025 that this does not cover prescriptions written outside Tasmania. Since March 2025 Victorian magistrates can decide not to cancel the licence of an unimpaired patient, a news report says.
driving.citation: healthdirect (reviewed Feb 2026); ACT Policing; Better Health Channel, Victoria; NSW Government release, Jun 25 2026; Road Safety (Alcohol and Drugs) Act 1970 (Tas) s. 6A; SA Hansard, Mar 5 2025; CarExpert, Sep 21 2026 (news)

border.short: No, except prescribed medicine you carry yourself
border.detail: Cannabis cannot be brought into Australia without permission. The Australian Border Force has warned that cannabis and CBD products imported without approval from the Office of Drug Control are seized and the importer may be prosecuted, and that they cannot come in under the personal importation scheme. A traveller can carry prescribed medicinal cannabis under the traveller's exemption: up to three months' supply for yourself or an immediate family member travelling with you, with a prescription from a medical practitioner, in its original packaging and ready to declare on arrival. The New South Wales Government's medicinal cannabis site warns that the medicine must have been supplied under that prescription, and that cannabis obtained another way may not meet the import rules. Inside Australia the ACT's rules end at its border: possessing cannabis in New South Wales is an offence.
border.citation: Australian Border Force release, Jul 5 2021; Office of Drug Control, Travelling with medicines; NSW Government, Travelling with cannabis medicine; Better Health Channel, Victoria (reviewed 2019); ACT Government, Cannabis

experiment.text: New South Wales is changing its drug-driving law for patients. A bill that passed both houses on September 17, 2026 lets patients with an unrestricted licence register with Transport for NSW, show a valid prescription and complete an online course. A registered patient whose lab result is under 50 nanograms of THC per millilitre of saliva faces no action. At or above that, the first two detections in two years bring warnings and a third brings a fine and a suspension of at least three months. Learner, provisional and commercial drivers are excluded, and a positive roadside test still means 24 hours off the road. Reports in late September said the law was awaiting assent and a start date, with registration expected in late 2026 or early 2027. We could not confirm that it has started.

differences.title: What is different about Australia
points: Six states and two territories each write their own drug laws, with Commonwealth law on top, so the answer changes when you cross a state line.
The ACT is the only place where adults may have and grow cannabis, and it never legalised buying. Selling, sharing and gifting, plants and seeds included, are still offences.
ACT home growers may not use hydroponics or other artificial cultivation, and no household may have more than four plants.

Commonwealth law still makes possession an offence in the ACT. ACT Policing says its officers can use either law. A University of New South Wales explainer reports the view that a Commonwealth prosecution is unlikely in practice.
South Australia and the Northern Territory fine small amounts instead of prosecuting. Other states rely on police cautions and diversion, each with its own gram limit.
Medicinal cannabis is dispensed by ordinary pharmacies, but most products are unapproved medicines and only one, for epilepsy, is subsidised.

A prescription does not protect a driver from a positive roadside test in New South Wales or Victoria. Tasmania's law has an exception for prescribed use, and New South Wales passed a registration scheme for patients in September 2026.
A bill to legalise cannabis nationally was voted down in the Senate on November 27, 2024, 24 votes to 13, after a Senate committee recommended in May 2024 that it not pass.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.summary: Illegal for adult use. A 2020 referendum to legalise it failed by about two points. Possession is a crime on paper, but police are told to weigh a health approach and rarely charge it on its own. Medicinal cannabis has been available on prescription since April 2020.
NZ.note: Dollar amounts are New Zealand dollars.

adult-use.short: No. A 2020 vote to legalise it failed narrowly
adult-use.detail: Cannabis is a controlled drug under the Misuse of Drugs Act 1975, and using or possessing it is an offence. On October 17, 2020 voters were asked whether they supported the proposed Cannabis Legalisation and Control Bill. The official count was 50.7% against and 48.4% in favour, a gap of 67,662 votes out of 2.9 million.
adult-use.citation: Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 s. 7, via the Community Law Manual; New Zealand Gazette notice 2020-au5131

medical.short: Yes, on prescription since April 2020
medical.detail: The Medicinal Cannabis Scheme began on April 1, 2020. Products are available only on prescription; the Ministry of Health names doctors, nurse practitioners and pharmacist prescribers, and no specialist recommendation is needed. Every product must be verified as meeting a minimum quality standard. Apart from two approved medicines, Sativex and Epidyolex, they are not approved medicines, which means their safety and efficacy have not been assessed. Dried flower can be prescribed for vaporising or for making tea, not for smoking. CBD products are prescription medicines too. No medicinal cannabis product was funded by Pharmac, the national medicines funder, as of February 2025.
medical.citation: Ministry of Health, information for consumers and minimum quality standard pages; bpacnz overview (updated Feb 2025)

buying.detail: No shop may sell cannabis. Selling any amount is dealing, which carries up to eight years in prison. The only legal supply is a medicinal product dispensed on prescription, and having one sent to you from overseas is against the law.
buying.citation: Community Law Manual (Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 s. 6); Ministry of Health, information for consumers

possession.short: No legal amount; up to 3 months or a NZ$500 fine
possession.detail: There is no legal amount. Possession carries a maximum of three months in prison, a fine of up to NZ$500, or both. A judge can jail someone only because of previous convictions or exceptional circumstances, and a first conviction usually means a fine. A 2019 amendment requires police to use discretion about prosecuting, and the Community Law Manual says a charge for possession alone is rare: a warning is more likely, and a first offender may be offered diversion. Holding 28 grams or 100 joints creates a presumption of dealing.
possession.citation: Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 s. 7 and Schedule 5, via the Community Law Manual (2026); bpacnz overview

sharing.short: No. Giving it to an adult is punished like possession
sharing.detail: Giving cannabis to someone 18 or older is treated like possession, with a fine of up to NZ$500 for a first offence. Selling it to anyone, or giving it to someone under 18, is dealing, with a maximum of eight years in prison.
sharing.citation: Community Law Manual (Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 ss. 6 and 7)

home-grow.short: No. Growing is a crime
home-grow.detail: Cultivating cannabis carries a maximum of seven years in prison. The Community Law Manual says a small grow for personal use usually ends in a fine or a community sentence, while commercial growing starts at two to four years. The medicinal scheme covers licensed commercial growing, and the Ministry of Health's patient page describes no allowance for growing your own.
home-grow.citation: Community Law Manual (Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 s. 9); Ministry of Health, information for consumers

driving.short: Random saliva tests; NZ$200 and 50 demerit points
driving.detail: Police can stop any driver for a saliva test that screens for THC, methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine. Testing began in Wellington on December 15, 2025 and has run nationwide since July 1, 2026. Two positive roadside tests mean a 12-hour driving ban, and a sample goes to a laboratory. A lab result over the limit for one drug brings a NZ$200 fine and 50 demerit points; two or more drugs, or refusing the test, bring NZ$400 and 75 points. The NZ Drug Foundation puts the THC thresholds at 15 nanograms per millilitre for the roadside screen and 5 for the lab. Patients who used a prescribed product as directed can apply for a medical defence after a notice arrives, but it does not lift the 12-hour ban. Driving while impaired is illegal in its own right, and an officer with good cause can order an impairment test and then a blood test.
driving.citation: NZ Drug Foundation, Roadside drug testing (as of Dec 16 2025); Radio 1XX citing New Zealand Police, Jul 17 2026 (news); bpacnz overview

record-relief.short: Concealed after 7 clean years, never erased
record-relief.detail: There is no cannabis-specific expungement. Under the Clean Slate scheme, convictions are concealed automatically once a person has gone seven years without a conviction, was never sentenced to custody, has paid every court-ordered fine and meets the other conditions. They can then say they have no convictions when asked in New Zealand. The record is hidden, not deleted, it comes back after any new conviction, and the scheme does not apply outside New Zealand, so another country may still ask for the full record.
record-relief.citation: Ministry of Justice, Clean Slate scheme (last updated Sep 9 2026)

border.short: No, except prescribed medicine declared on arrival
border.detail: A traveller may bring a medicinal cannabis product into New Zealand only if it was prescribed to them, they carry a copy of the prescription or a letter from the prescriber, it is in its original labelled container and they declare it on the passenger arrival card. The limit is three months' supply of a CBD product or one month's supply of any other medicinal cannabis product. Having a product sent to you from overseas is against the law. When leaving, check every destination and transit country: the Ministry of Health warns that some treat possession as a crime with no medical exemption.
border.citation: Ministry of Health, Medicinal cannabis: information for consumers

experiment.text: Roadside testing is new and still small. From the first tests in Wellington in December 2025 to June 30, 2026, police ran 4,143 roadside screening tests and 134 came back positive, about 3.2%, according to a July 2026 radio news report citing police. THC may show in saliva for about 12 hours in people who use cannabis occasionally and up to 72 hours in frequent users, the NZ Drug Foundation says, citing studies, and detection varies widely.

differences.title: What is different about New Zealand
points: New Zealand put legalisation to a national vote and it lost by 67,662 votes, 50.7% to 48.4%, on October 17, 2020.
Possession can still mean three months in prison on paper, but the law has required police discretion since 2019 and charges for possession alone are rare.
At 28 grams or 100 joints the law presumes you are dealing, and it is up to you to prove otherwise.
Giving cannabis to another adult is punished like possession. Selling any amount, or giving it to someone under 18, is dealing, with up to eight years in prison.
Prescribed flower is for a vaporiser or for tea. A prescription cannot be for a product meant to be smoked.
A 2018 law change gave terminally ill patients a legal defence for possessing illicit cannabis, according to bpacnz, a clinical guidance body.
Random roadside saliva testing went nationwide on July 1, 2026. A prescription can cancel the fine afterwards but not the 12-hour driving ban at the roadside.
Old convictions are concealed, not erased, after seven conviction-free years, and the Clean Slate scheme stops at the border.

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.summary: Adults may use, have and grow cannabis in private because of a 2018 Constitutional Court ruling. Selling it is still a crime, and a 2024 law that would set the rules was signed but has not started. Medicines with THC are reached mostly through special permits.
ZA.note: The Cannabis for Private Purposes Act of 2024 is signed but not yet in force, so this page separates the rules that apply now from the ones waiting to start. Amounts are in South African rand.

adult-use.short: Yes, in private, since a 2018 court ruling
adult-use.detail: On September 18, 2018 the Constitutional Court ruled in the Prince case that it is unconstitutional to make it a crime for an adult to use or possess cannabis in private for their own consumption, or to grow it in a private place for that purpose. The court said privacy reaches beyond the home. Using or possessing it in public, and any use by a child, stayed illegal. Parliament passed the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act in 2024 to put the ruling into law. It starts on a date the President sets by proclamation, and an October 2026 column in Business Day said it was still not in effect.
adult-use.citation: Constitutional Court, Prince [2018] ZACC 30 (media summary); Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 7 of 2024 s. 8; Business Day, Oct 27 2026 (opinion)

medical.short: Prescription, mostly through special permits
medical.detail: THC is a Schedule 6 medicine and CBD a Schedule 4 medicine, so both need a prescription. A pharmacist and pharmacologist writing in December 2025 said no THC-containing product had yet been registered in South Africa, so patients reach THC medicines through section 21 permits for unregistered products, and the regulator does not publish how many permits it issues. Low-dose CBD products, up to 20 mg a day, can be sold as complementary medicines.
medical.citation: Spotlight, Dr Andy Gray, Dec 3 2025 (news column)

buying.detail: The 2018 ruling did not legalise selling, and the 2024 Act keeps dealing a crime, with up to 10 years in prison. The medicines regulator has licensed no retail outlets for cannabis, and its cultivation permits do not allow sales to the public, so shops that call themselves licensed dispensaries are operating illegally, the Spotlight column says.
buying.citation: Constitutional Court, Prince (media summary); Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 7 of 2024 s. 4; Spotlight, Dec 3 2025 (news column)

possession.short: No set amount yet. Draft rules propose 750 grams
possession.detail: For now there is no legal amount. The court left it to Parliament to set what counts as personal use, and police judge each case by the circumstances, including the quantity. If they suspect dealing they can arrest, and a court decides. Draft regulations published for comment in February 2026 propose up to 750 grams in a private place, and 750 grams a day in public if it is kept out of sight. Under the 2024 Act, once it starts, having more than the prescribed amount could bring up to five years in prison.
possession.citation: Constitutional Court, Prince (media summary); Adams & Adams on the draft regulations, Feb 2026 (law firm); Cannabis for Private Purposes Act s. 4; EWN, Aug 21 2026

sharing.short: Not yet. The 2024 law would allow free sharing
sharing.detail: The 2018 ruling covered using, possessing and growing for your own consumption. It did not cover selling or supplying anyone. Once in force, the 2024 Act lets one adult give cannabis to another in private with no payment or exchange of any kind. Giving it to a child is a crime unless a medical practitioner prescribed it.
sharing.citation: Constitutional Court, Prince (media summary); Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 7 of 2024 ss. 2 and 3

home-grow.short: Yes, in private. Draft rules propose 5 plants
home-grow.detail: Adults may grow cannabis in a private place for their own consumption in private. No plant limit is in force yet. The February 2026 draft regulations propose five plants per adult at any one time, regardless of size or strain. A lawyer quoted in August 2026 said the rules still need to make clear whether limits apply per person or per household.
home-grow.citation: Constitutional Court, Prince (media summary); Adams & Adams on the draft regulations (law firm); EWN, Aug 21 2026

driving.short: Illegal while under the influence; no THC limit yet
